problems.problem: Safety investigators need better tooling to investigate harmful behavior and take consistent enforcement actions across multiple product and platform surfaces.
evidence: the systems that humans — and increasingly Claude — use to investigate potential harms and take enforcement actions across Anthropic's first-party products and third-party cloud platforms
you'll own the tools our safety investigators rely on to understand what's happening on our platforms and act on it
Build investigation, review, and enforcement tooling for both first-party and third-party platform surfaces
problems.rationale: The emphasis on investigation views, case queues, audit logging, and account actioning indicates that existing cross-surface enforcement workflows are insufficient or fragmented.

problems.problem: The organization lacks a reusable platform that allows new review workflows to be created quickly and safely.
evidence: This is a foundational role: as one of the first engineers on this new team
Develop the platform layer of reusable APIs, data storage, and backend services that lets new review workflows be stood up quickly and safely
a sandbox environment where new review interfaces and workflows can be built and iterated quickly
problems.rationale: Calling the team new and foundational, while explicitly requiring reusable services and a sandbox, signals a need to establish core infrastructure rather than merely extend a mature platform.

problems.problem: Human review capacity will not scale with model capabilities and usage without effective automation that preserves appropriate human judgment.
evidence: As model capabilities and usage grow, you'll also drive how we scale review through automation
building systems where Claude meaningfully extends what human reviewers can do, while keeping people in the loop where their judgment matters most
Scale review through automation, including enabling reviewers to use Claude effectively and building toward Claude-assisted and Claude-driven review workflows
problems.rationale: The listing directly identifies growing review demand and the need to augment or automate reviewer work while retaining human oversight.

problems.problem: Enforcement decisions and review operations need to become faster, more accurate, and more measurable.
evidence: the speed, clarity, and reliability of this tooling directly determines how quickly Anthropic can identify harmful behavior, make sound enforcement decisions, and feed signal back into model training
translate enforcement and investigation needs into reliable, well-designed systems that measurably reduce handling time and decision error
Instrument the tools you ship — surfacing metrics on queue health, reviewer throughput, and decision quality
problems.rationale: The focus on handling time, decision error, queue health, throughput, and decision quality shows that current review processes need stronger operational performance and feedback measurement.

problems.problem: Sensitive review workflows must satisfy stringent privacy, access-control, auditability, and data-retention requirements.
evidence: privacy-preserving primitives that keep review workflows compatible with our data retention commitments
Build in the guardrails that sensitive internal tools require: granular permissions, audit trails, data-access controls
ensure tooling evolves alongside new privacy primitives and data retention commitments
problems.rationale: These requirements indicate that the company needs tooling capable of supporting enforcement operations without violating privacy, governance, or retention constraints.

problems.problem: Reviewers need protection from harmful content exposure and other wellbeing risks while performing their work.
evidence: reviewer wellbeing features such as content obfuscation and exposure limits
Build in the guardrails that sensitive internal tools require
problems.rationale: The explicit requirement for obfuscation and exposure limits shows that reviewer wellbeing and the risks of repeated harmful-content exposure are unresolved operational concerns.
